st.2: A deadlock between the two Houses is resolved by a joint sitting under Article 108.
st.4: Where State ratification is needed, State legislatures ratify it by a special majority.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: there is no joint sitting on a Constitution Amendment Bill. Statement 4 is wrong: States ratify by a simple majority.

st.2: The second House must return an ordinary Bill within 14 days.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the 14-day limit applies to a Money Bill in the Rajya Sabha, not to an ordinary Bill.

st.1: The forms of oath of the President, the Vice-President and the Governor are contained in the Third Schedule.

x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: their oaths are in Articles 60, 69 and 159, not the Third Schedule.

st.2: Fakhruddin Ali Ahmed was the first President of India to die in office.
st.4: Neelam Sanjiva Reddy served as Vice-President before becoming President.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the first President to die in office was Dr Zakir Husain (1969); Fakhruddin Ali Ahmed was the second. Statement 4 is wrong: Sanjiva Reddy was never Vice-President.

st.1: The 44th Amendment made ministerial advice binding on the President, and the 42nd Amendment let him return it once for reconsideration.
st.2: During a National Emergency the advice of the Council of Ministers ceases to bind the President.
st.4: Administering the oath of office to Union Ministers is one of the Prime Minister's duties under Article 78.

x: Only statement 3 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the 42nd Amendment made advice binding and the 44th allowed one return. Statement 2 is wrong: the advice binds the President even during an Emergency. Statement 4 is wrong: the President administers the oath to Ministers.

st.1: Under Article 88, a Minister who is a member of the Rajya Sabha can take part in the proceedings of the Lok Sabha and also vote there.
st.2: Under Article 75(3), the Council of Ministers is collectively responsible to both Houses of Parliament.

x: Only statement 3 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: such a Minister may speak in the Lok Sabha but cannot vote there. Statement 2 is wrong: collective responsibility is to the Lok Sabha only.

st.3: The power is a relic of the Indian Councils Act, 1909.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the ordinance power comes from the Government of India Act, 1935.

st.2: He must be qualified to be appointed a judge of the Supreme Court.
st.4: Like the Attorney General, he has the right of audience in all courts in India.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: he must be qualified to be a High Court judge. Statement 4 is wrong: his right of audience is in all courts within the State only.

st.2: It limited a State Council of Ministers to 15 per cent of the total strength of both Houses of the State Legislature, subject to a minimum of 12 Ministers.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the 15 per cent cap is on the strength of the Legislative Assembly only, with a minimum of 12 Ministers.

st.1: Parliament can change the number of judges only by a constitutional amendment under Article 368.
st.3: The 2026 Ordinance that raised it to 38 including the CJI was promulgated under Article 213.

x: Only statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the number is fixed by an ordinary law, the Supreme Court (Number of Judges) Act, 1956, under Article 124(1). Statement 3 is wrong: a central ordinance is made by the President under Article 123; Article 213 is the Governor's power.

st.1: The term 'judicial review' is expressly used in Article 13.
st.3: The doctrine originated in Marbury v. Madison (1803), decided under US Chief Justice Earl Warren.

x: Statements 2 and 4 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the term 'judicial review' is not used anywhere in the Constitution. Statement 3 is wrong: Marbury v. Madison was decided under Chief Justice John Marshall.

st.3: The Indian Forest Service was created by the original Constitution itself, along with the IAS and the IPS.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: only the IAS and IPS were deemed created by Article 312; the Indian Forest Service was created by Parliament in 1966.

st.3: It reduced the States' share in the divisible pool to 40%.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the 16th Finance Commission retained the States' share at 41%.

st.1: Being found guilty in a civil case is a ground for removal.
st.4: For misbehaviour, Parliament must also pass an address by special majority.

x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the grounds are insolvency, paid outside employment and infirmity of mind or body, not a civil case. Statement 4 is wrong: removal for misbehaviour needs only the President's order after the Supreme Court's enquiry; no address by Parliament.

st.1: It is a statutory body created by the Delhi Special Police Establishment Act, 1946.

x: Statements 2, 3 and 4 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the CBI was set up by a Home Ministry resolution (1963) and is not a statutory body; it draws its powers from the DSPE Act.

st.2: Its 47 members are elected by the UN Security Council for three-year terms.
st.3: A member can serve any number of consecutive terms.

x: Statements 1 and 4 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the 47 members are elected by the UN General Assembly for three-year terms. Statement 3 is wrong: a member can serve at most two consecutive terms.

st.1: The Indian Civil Liberties Union was founded in 1936 by B.R. Ambedkar.

x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the Indian Civil Liberties Union was founded in August 1936 by Jawaharlal Nehru and others, not Ambedkar.

st.1: The National Commission for Backward Classes got constitutional status under Article 338A.
st.4: The headquarters of the NHRC is in Mumbai.

x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the NCBC is under Article 338B (102nd Amendment, 2018); Article 338A is the NCST. Statement 4 is wrong: the NHRC is headquartered in New Delhi.

st.3: It inquires only into subjects in the State List.
st.4: It may inquire into a matter already being inquired into by the NHRC.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: an SHRC covers subjects in both the State List and the Concurrent List. Statement 4 is wrong: it does not take up a matter the NHRC is already inquiring into.

st.2: It is a statutory body created by the Delhi Special Police Establishment Act, 1946.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the CBI was set up by an executive resolution in 1963 and is not a statutory body; it only draws its powers from the DSPE Act.

st.1: The Chief Justice of the High Court is a member of the recommending committee.
st.4: The Governor may remove a State Information Commissioner for proved misbehaviour after an inquiry by the High Court.

x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the committee is the Chief Minister, the Leader of the Opposition and a Cabinet Minister; no judge sits on it. Statement 4 is wrong: removal for misbehaviour follows an inquiry by the Supreme Court.

st.4: The Krishna River Management Board set fresh terms of reference for KWDT-II on the AP-Telangana dispute in October 2023.

x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 4 is wrong: the fresh terms of reference (October 2023) were set by the Centre, not the KRMB.

st.1: The first general elections in India were conducted under Chief Election Commissioner T.N. Seshan.
st.2: Lok Sabha and Assembly elections were held simultaneously only in the first general election of 1951-52.

x: Only statement 3 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the first general elections (1951-52) were held under Sukumar Sen. Statement 2 is wrong: simultaneous polls were held in the first four general elections, up to 1967.

st.2: A registered-unrecognised party may hold a reserved symbol of its own.
st.3: Two recognised parties in different States cannot hold the same reserved symbol.

x: Statements 1 and 4 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: reserved symbols are only for recognised parties; an unrecognised party can at most get a common free symbol. Statement 3 is wrong: two recognised parties in different States may hold the same reserved symbol.

st.1: In practice, functionaries meant to serve Panchayats mostly report to the Panchayats themselves.
st.2: Funds reaching Panchayats are mostly untied, matching their functions.

x: Only statement 3 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: such functionaries mostly report to State line departments. Statement 2 is wrong: Panchayat funds are mostly tied and do not match their functions.

st.3: The National Panchayat Awards do not use the Panchayat Advancement Index in their assessment.
st.4: Karnataka's People's Plan Campaign was launched in 1996.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the awards do use the Panchayat Advancement Index. Statement 4 is wrong: the People's Plan Campaign of 1996 was Kerala's.

st.1: Municipalities are graded as Special, Selection, Grade I, II and III on the basis of population.

x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: AP municipalities are graded on the basis of annual income, not population.

st.2: Women form about one-third of the elected Panchayat representatives in India.

x: Statements 1, 3 and 4 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: women are about 46% of elected Panchayat representatives, well above the one-third minimum.

st.2: Scheduled Tribes, like Other Traditional Forest Dwellers, must show three generations (75 years) of residence.
st.3: Rights are heritable and alienable, up to a ceiling of 4 hectares per family.

x: Statements 1 and 4 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: only Other Traditional Forest Dwellers must show three generations (75 years); forest-dwelling STs need not. Statement 3 is wrong: rights are heritable but not alienable.

st.1: It recommended that PPP contracts should never be renegotiated.
st.3: It encouraged public sector undertakings to bid for toll PPPs.
st.4: It encouraged the Swiss-challenge method.

x: Only statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: Kelkar wanted a built-in renegotiation mechanism. Statement 3 is wrong: it discouraged PSUs from bidding for PPPs. Statement 4 is wrong: it discouraged the Swiss-challenge method.

st.2: The GGI is revised every year and 'foreign affairs' is one of its ten sectors.
st.3: In GGI 2021, Andhra Pradesh ranked first overall and Gujarat ranked first in agriculture and allied sectors.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the GGI is revised every two years and foreign affairs is not one of its ten sectors. Statement 3 is wrong: Gujarat ranked first overall and Andhra Pradesh first in agriculture and allied sectors.

st.2: Under the AP Reorganisation Act, 2014, the Telangana ERC stayed joint regulator for not more than six months.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: it was APERC that acted as the joint regulator for not more than six months.

st.3: Consumers International has its headquarters at Geneva.

x: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: Consumers International is headquartered in London.

st.2: The admissibility of a complaint must be decided within 21 days, failing which it is deemed rejected.
st.3: No fee is charged for complaints of any value.
st.4: A person who buys goods for resale is a consumer.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: if admissibility is not decided within 21 days the complaint is deemed admitted. Statement 3 is wrong: only complaints up to Rs 5 lakh are free. Statement 4 is wrong: a buyer for resale or commercial purpose is not a consumer.

st.1: Its temporary office in April 2026 was at Siripuram.

x: All three statements are correct: SCoR's temporary office was at Siripuram (the zonal HQ is coming up at Mudasarlova), the gazette notification came on 4 May 2026, and it became fully working as the 18th zone on 1 June 2026.

All three statements are correct: the G-33 (2003) pursues food security, the SSM and special products; the G-90 combines the African Group, ACP and LDCs; and the SSM lets developing countries raise tariffs against import surges.

st.2: Under it, the MGNREGA job cards continue unchanged.
st.3: Only the Centre may pause work for up to 60 days during the sowing and harvest seasons.
st.4: Its wage floor of ₹300 per day (2026-27) is indexed to the CPI for Industrial Workers.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: job cards are replaced by Gramin Rozgar Guarantee Cards. Statement 3 is wrong: it is the States that may pause work for up to 60 days. Statement 4 is wrong: the wage floor is indexed to the CPI for Agricultural Labourers.

st.2: The annual premium of PMJJBY was raised from ₹12 to ₹20 from 1 June 2022.
st.3: PMSBY gives ₹2 lakh for accidental death or total disability and also covers natural death.
st.4: PMJJBY has more enrolments than PMSBY.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the ₹12-to-₹20 rise was for PMSBY; PMJJBY costs ₹436. Statement 3 is wrong: PMSBY covers only accidental death or disability (₹1 lakh for partial); natural death is PMJJBY's. Statement 4 is wrong: PMSBY has more enrolments.

st.1: Critical Gap Funding covers the entire project cost.

x: Statements 2, 3 and 4 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: Critical Gap Funding is only up to 30% of the project cost.

st.1: The Desert Development Programme (1977-78) covers only hot deserts.
st.2: 'Garibi Hatao' was first introduced in the Fourth Five Year Plan.

x: Only statement 3 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the DDP covers both hot and cold deserts. Statement 2 is wrong: Garibi Hatao entered planning with the Fifth Five Year Plan.

st.1: The unit assistance is ₹1.20 lakh in both plains and hilly or difficult areas.
st.2: Beneficiaries are identified from Census 2011 data and verified by the Gram Sabha.
st.4: In August 2024 NITI Aayog approved 2 crore more houses for 2024-25 to 2028-29.

x: Only statement 3 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: hilly and difficult areas get ₹1.30 lakh. Statement 2 is wrong: beneficiaries come from the SECC 2011 data, not the Census. Statement 4 is wrong: the 2 crore additional houses were approved by the Union Cabinet.

st.3: Sanjeevani, statewide from August 2026, gives every citizen a digital health profile and an Aarogyasri card.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: Sanjeevani gives a digital health profile with an ABHA ID, not an Aarogyasri card.

st.1: Under YSR Kalyanamasthu, the ₹1 lakh aid is for BC brides.
st.3: Under Kalyanamasthu and Shaadi Tohfa, only the bride must have passed SSC.
st.4: Chandranna Pelli Kanuka (2014-19) gave aid only to minority brides.

x: Only statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: ₹1 lakh is for SC/ST brides; BC brides get ₹50,000. Statement 3 is wrong: both bride and groom must have passed SSC. Statement 4 is wrong: Chandranna Pelli Kanuka gave ₹75,000 for SC inter-caste marriages, among others.

st.1: It was prepared by NITI Aayog.
st.3: Andhra Pradesh had the highest relative per capita income in 2023-24.

x: Only statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the report is the EAC-PM's, by Sanjeev Sanyal and Aakanksha Arora. Statement 3 is wrong: Delhi had the highest relative per capita income (250.8), not Andhra Pradesh.

st.1: Interest earned on a productive loan is a transfer payment and is excluded.
st.3: Change in inventories is excluded because the goods have not been sold.
st.4: Profits of public enterprises are excluded because they accrue to the State.

x: Only statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: such interest is a factor payment and is included. Statement 3 is wrong: change in inventories is part of output and is included. Statement 4 is wrong: profits of public enterprises are factor income and are included.

st.4: India ranks among the top ten on the Economic Complexity Index.

x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 4 is wrong: India ranks only 44th on the Economic Complexity Index.
All three statements are correct: Dantwala (1970) rejected a single number, Bhagwati (1973) reviewed unemployment estimates, and the 2017 Standing Committee designed the PLFS.

st.4: Its first annual report, for 2017-18, was released by the Labour Bureau.

x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 4 is wrong: the first PLFS annual report (2017-18) was released by the NSO of MoSPI, in 2019.

st.3: The Rangarajan group fixed calorie norms of 2,400 kcal rural and 2,100 kcal urban.
st.4: The Rangarajan group used a single urban poverty line basket for both rural and urban areas.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: 2,400/2,100 kcal were the older (Alagh/Lakdawala) norms; Rangarajan used about 2,155 and 2,090 kcal. Statement 4 is wrong: the single urban basket was Tendulkar's; Rangarajan returned to separate rural and urban baskets.

st.1: GST 2.0 (August 2025) abolished the special slab for sin and luxury goods.
st.2: It is an origin-based tax, and input tax credit ends cascading.

x: Only statement 3 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: GST 2.0 created a special 40% slab for sin and luxury goods. Statement 2 is wrong: GST is destination-based.

st.3: It continued revenue-deficit grants to States.
st.4: Disaster funding is shared 75:25 for all States, including the North-Eastern and Himalayan States.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the 16th Finance Commission ended revenue-deficit grants. Statement 4 is wrong: North-Eastern and Himalayan States share 90:10; 75:25 is for the others.

st.3: It was never replaced by an Act.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the Ordinance was replaced by the AP Microfinance Institutions Act, 2011.

st.1: In 2020 the Delhi High Court struck down the RBI's 2018 circular barring banks from dealing with crypto businesses.
st.2: The Finance Act, 2022 made cryptocurrency legal tender in India.

x: Only statement 3 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the RBI circular was struck down by the Supreme Court (IAMAI case, 2020). Statement 2 is wrong: the Finance Act, 2022 only taxed virtual digital assets; crypto is not legal tender.

st.2: Open Market Operations are the RBI's main tool for managing day-to-day (frictional) liquidity.
st.3: Surplus liquidity in the banking system pulls money-market rates above the repo rate.

x: Statements 1 and 4 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: OMOs manage durable liquidity; day-to-day liquidity is handled through the LAF. Statement 3 is wrong: surplus liquidity pulls money-market rates below the repo rate.

st.1: In August 2026 India had about 1.81 lakh bank branches and 58.77 crore Atal Pension Yojana accounts.

x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the 58.77 crore accounts are PMJDY accounts, not Atal Pension Yojana accounts.
Both are correct: inflation from higher government spending together with falling industrial output and slow growth produce stagflation.

st.1: CPI inflation was 2.2%, the highest in 12 years.
st.3: Food inflation was higher than headline inflation.

x: Only statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: 2.2% was a 12-year low, not a high. Statement 3 is wrong: with food prices falling (-0.2%), food inflation was below headline inflation.

st.1: Defence services
st.3: Border roads
st.4: Pensions

x: Only 2 is developmental: irrigation and flood control is developmental, while defence services, border roads (a defence item) and pensions are non-developmental expenditure.

st.2: Under-priced irrigation water is an explicit subsidy.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: under-priced irrigation water is a hidden (implicit) subsidy.

st.1: Fixing the policy repo rate is one of the objectives of the Act.
st.2: The FRBM Bill was introduced in 2000, when Manmohan Singh was the Finance Minister.

x: Only statement 3 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the repo rate is set by the RBI's MPC; the FRBM Act deals with fiscal targets. Statement 2 is wrong: the Bill was introduced by Yashwant Sinha.

st.3: Income terms of trade = NTT × import quantity index.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: income terms of trade = NTT × export quantity index.

st.1: It is released by NITI Aayog.
st.2: Andhra Pradesh was placed in the 'Exemplar' category among coastal states.

x: Only statement 3 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: LEADS is released by DPIIT, Ministry of Commerce and Industry. Statement 2 is wrong: Andhra Pradesh was an 'Accelerator'; Tamil Nadu was the 'Exemplar'.

st.1: FEMA was first proposed in the Union Budget of 1997-98 as a criminal law, like FERA.

x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: FEMA, proposed in the 1997-98 Budget, is a civil law, unlike the criminal FERA.

st.2: A swap has a tenor of 3 months and cannot be rolled over.
st.4: The first INR drawdown under it was made by Sri Lanka in April 2026.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the 3-month swap can be rolled over twice. Statement 4 is wrong: the first INR drawdown (April 2026) was by the Maldives.

st.2: During April 2000 – March 2015 the RBI's New Delhi regional office received the largest cumulative FDI.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the Mumbai regional office received the largest cumulative FDI, ahead of New Delhi.

st.2: Foreign investment of 10% or more of the post-issue paid-up equity of a listed company is generally classed as FDI.

x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: in an unlisted company any stake by a person resident outside India is FDI; the 10% test applies only to listed companies.

st.3: India's target weight in the JP Morgan Emerging Market bond index is 15%.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: India's target weight in the JP Morgan EM bond index is 10%.

st.3: Land ceiling legislation is one of the principal areas of the WTO Agreement on Agriculture.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the AoA's three pillars are market access, domestic support and export subsidies; land ceilings are not among them.

st.3: Agricultural exports reached a record US$ 51.91 billion, more than half of India's merchandise exports.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the record US$ 51.91 billion of farm exports was only about 11.86% of merchandise exports.

st.2: It is administered by the Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare.
st.4: It covers about 81 crore people, all of them in rural areas.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the NFSA is run by the Department of Food and Public Distribution. Statement 4 is wrong: its about 81 crore beneficiaries include up to 50% of the urban population.
Both statements are correct: GLC in FY25 was about Rs 28.69 lakh crore against a Rs 27.50 lakh crore target, and the South gets about 48% of farm credit with about 17% of the cropped area.

st.2: It is a virtual market that replaces the physical APMC mandis.
st.3: Its lead implementing agency is NABARD.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: e-NAM links the existing APMC mandis online; it does not replace them. Statement 3 is wrong: its lead agency is the Small Farmers' Agribusiness Consortium (SFAC).

All four statements are correct: industry is about 25.3% of GVA, manufacturing's real share has held at 17-18%, the public sector is about 13-14% of GDP, and medium- and high-tech is about 46.3% of manufacturing.

st.3: Iron ore is the main imported input of India's steel industry.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: India has ample iron ore; the main imported input of the steel industry is coking coal.

st.1: It was launched on 25 September 2014 with NITI Aayog as the nodal body.
st.2: Its logo is a tiger made of cogwheels.

x: Only statement 3 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the nodal ministry is Commerce and Industry (DPIIT). Statement 2 is wrong: the logo is a lion made of cogwheels.

st.2: It aimed to create 100 million additional jobs in the services sector.
st.4: It is limited to a single sector, electronics.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the 100 million additional jobs were to be in manufacturing. Statement 4 is wrong: the policy is sector-, location- and technology-neutral.

st.2: NITI Aayog's Investment Friendliness Index (July 2026) is compiled by the Asian Competitiveness Institute.
st.3: In the ACI Ease of Doing Business Index 2018, Maharashtra was 1st, up from 5th in 2016.

x: Statements 1 and 4 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the Investment Friendliness Index (8 pillars) is NITI Aayog's own. Statement 3 is wrong: Andhra Pradesh was 1st in ACI 2018 (up from 5th), with Maharashtra 2nd.
All four are correct: the Industrial Policy Resolution of 1948 listed raw materials, finance, marketing and technology as handicaps.

st.2: Royalties are tax revenue of the State.
st.3: Profits and dividends of State PSUs are tax revenue of the State.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: royalties are own non-tax revenue. Statement 3 is wrong: profits and dividends of State PSUs are also non-tax revenue.

st.3: The Power Ministry's order of August 2022 asked Andhra Pradesh to pay Telangana within 30 days.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the August 2022 order asked Telangana to pay Andhra Pradesh (about ₹6,757 crore) within 30 days.

st.2: Centrally Sponsored Schemes are funded 60:40 for SCS States against 90:10 for others.
st.3: SCS for Andhra Pradesh is provided in the AP Reorganisation Act, 2014.

x: Statements 1 and 4 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: SCS States get 90:10 and others 60:40. Statement 3 is wrong: SCS for AP was a Prime Minister's assurance in the Rajya Sabha, not a provision of the Act.

st.2: Cooperatives today face no shortage of professional management or digital capacity.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: many cooperatives still lack professional management and digital capacity.

st.2: Under APFAMGS, supported by the World Bank, farmers collect rainfall and well data and prepare crop-water budgets.
st.3: The area irrigated per well is rising as 40,000-50,000 new bore wells are dug every year.
st.4: The Jal Jeevan Mission set up AP's real-time groundwater monitoring.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: APFAMGS was supported by the FAO, not the World Bank. Statement 3 is wrong: with so many new bore wells the area irrigated per well is falling. Statement 4 is wrong: real-time groundwater monitoring came from the National Hydrology Project.

st.1: The Act named BPCL to examine a refinery, and BPCL's refinery is coming up near Ramayapatnam.
st.2: South Coast Railway became operational on 1 June 2026 with its headquarters at Vijayawada.

x: Only statement 3 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the Act named IOC or HPCL; the refinery coming up is BPCL's. Statement 2 is wrong: SCoR (operational 1 June 2026) is headquartered at Visakhapatnam.

st.3: Krishnapatnam is a major port.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: Krishnapatnam is a non-major private port (Adani).

st.2: The RMZ GCC Park in Visakhapatnam is at Kakinada.
st.3: The Kopparthy Electronics Manufacturing Cluster is in Kurnool district.

x: Statements 1 and 4 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the RMZ GCC Park is at Kapuluppada, Visakhapatnam. Statement 3 is wrong: Kopparthy EMC is in YSR Kadapa district.

st.2: Quantum Key Distribution (QKD) is not among its focus areas.
st.3: Its launch is scheduled for January 2026.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: QKD is one of its focus areas. Statement 3 is wrong: its launch is scheduled for January 2027.

st.2: Its drone survey covers agricultural land as well as village abadi areas.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: SVAMITVA maps only the inhabited abadi areas, not agricultural land.
Both statements are correct: AP's installed capacity was about 27,587 MW (July 2025), and India had about 500 MWh of battery storage against a need of 336 GWh by 2029-30.

st.4: Ending all development in ecologically sensitive areas is one of its objectives.

x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 4 is wrong: the NEP seeks to balance conservation and development; it does not aim to end all development in sensitive areas.

st.2: NavIC, a constellation of 7 satellites, times its signals with rubidium atomic clocks.

x: Both statements are correct: UTC is kept by caesium clocks, while NavIC satellites carry rubidium atomic clocks.

st.2: Oceanic crust is lighter than continental crust.
st.4: Aluminium is one of the main lighter elements of the Earth's core.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: basaltic oceanic crust is denser than continental crust. Statement 4 is wrong: the core is iron-nickel with light elements such as sulphur, oxygen and silicon; aluminium is a crustal element.

st.3: Basic (mafic) lava builds steep stratovolcanoes.

x: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: runny basic lava builds gently sloping shield volcanoes.

st.4: Chad lies in the Lake Chad basin, not the Nile basin.

x: All four statements are correct: South Sudan is landlocked with Juba as capital, the Pygmies live in the Congo basin, its peatland holds about 29 billion tonnes of carbon, and Chad lies in the Lake Chad basin.

st.3: In the Bergeron code, the second letter shows the temperature of the source region, such as T for tropical and P for polar.

x: All three statements are correct: an air mass is uniform in temperature and humidity, the first letter (c or m) shows moisture, and the second (T or P) shows temperature.

st.2: India gets tropical cyclones, not hurricanes, in the Bay of Bengal and the Arabian Sea.

x: All three statements are correct: the North-west Pacific typhoon region covers East Asia, the Philippines and Japan, India's storms are called cyclones, and Typhoon Noul hit Guangdong in July 2026.

st.2: The Kadapa–Kurnool zone receives about 75–100 cm.
